title: Inclusive Health Literacy Starts With Access
excerpt: Accessible health information empowers youth with disabilities to make informed choices and advocate for better services.
author: Twezuule Foundation

content.text: Young people with disabilities deserve health information in formats they can use. We co-design sessions with youth leaders to ensure language, format, and delivery are accessible.
When information is accessible, youth can make choices about their health with confidence and dignity.

title: Livelihoods With Dignity: Skills for Economic Independence
excerpt: Economic empowerment programs build sustainable income pathways that value talent, resilience, and leadership.
author: Twezuule Foundation

content.text: We provide skills training and mentorship that match local market opportunities. Participants co-create their learning plans and receive ongoing support.
Economic independence is about choice, security, and the power to shape your future.

title: Youth Leadership That Shapes Policy
excerpt: Civic participation is stronger when youth with disabilities lead policy conversations and community decisions.
author: Twezuule Foundation

content.text: Twezuule supports youth leaders to engage local councils, health boards, and community platforms. We invest in leadership skills and accessible civic spaces.
When youth lead, policies and services become more inclusive and responsive.
